title: Annular Majorana mode in a superconducting topological insulator
summary: When the surface states of a topological insulator becomes superconducting, topological superconductivity can be obtained, and each vortex on the surface can host one single Majorana zero-energy mode which is usually a wave packet decaying exponentially off the vortex core. Here, we predict stable Majorana zero-energy mode whose wave function is ring-shape, dubbed as annular Majorana mode, in the superconducting vortex in topological insulators respecting $3$-fold or $6$-fold rotational symmetry. Such topological insulators are featured with a single nonlinear Dirac cone located at $\barΓ$ or three linear Dirac cones at $\bar{\text{M}}$ in the surface Brillouin zone. The annular Majorana mode originates from the effective chiral $f$-wave superconductivity on the nonlinear Dirac cone in the former case and the interference of the effective chiral $p$-wave superconductivity on the three linear Dirac cones in the latter. In both cases, the annular Majorana mode is stabilized by the rotational symmetry and the winding number $3$ carried by the surface states. Candidate materials supporting the annular Majorana mode are predicted. Our work provides new insights into the topological superconductivity in superconducting topological insulators.

AI.tldr: The paper predicts a stable annular (ring-shaped) Majorana zero-energy mode in superconducting vortices on the surface of topological insulators with 3-fold or 6-fold rotational symmetry. This mode arises from effective chiral f-wave superconductivity on a single nonlinear Dirac cone (at Γ) or from interference of effective chiral p-wave superconductivity on three linear Dirac cones (at M), and is stabilized by rotational symmetry and winding number 3 carried by surface states.
AI.motivation: To discover and predict a new type of stable Majorana zero-energy mode with a ring-shaped wave function (annular Majorana mode) in superconducting topological insulators, going beyond the conventional exponentially-decaying vortex-core-localized Majorana modes.
AI.method: The authors analyze superconducting vortices on topological insulator surfaces with 3-fold (C3) or 6-fold (C6) rotational symmetry. They consider two classes of materials: those with a single nonlinear Dirac cone at the Γ point and those with three linear Dirac cones at the M points in the surface Brillouin zone. The annular Majorana mode is derived from effective chiral f-wave superconductivity in the former case, and from interference of effective chiral p-wave superconductivity on the three cones in the latter. Stability is ensured by rotational symmetry and winding number 3 of the surface states.
AI.result: Stable annular Majorana modes with ring-shaped wave functions are predicted in superconducting vortices of topological insulators with C3 or C6 rotational symmetry. The mode arises from chiral f-wave superconductivity on a nonlinear Dirac cone or interference of chiral p-wave superconductivity on three linear Dirac cones. Rotational symmetry and winding number 3 stabilize the mode. Candidate host materials are predicted.
AI.conclusion: This work provides new insights into topological superconductivity in superconducting topological insulators by establishing that Majorana zero modes need not be localized at the vortex core, but can form stable annular (ring-shaped) configurations protected by rotational symmetry and the topological winding of the surface states.

title: Topological Charge-Transfer Excitons
summary: Excitons possess internal structure absent from single-particle Bloch particles, allowing their band topology to emerge from the bound-state structure rather than being inherited from their constituents. This raises the question of how the internal structure of a bound state can provide a microscopic origin of exciton topology. Here we show that the real-space embedding of charge-transfer excitons can generate an intrinsic manifold of symmetry-related off-site composite orbitals whose coupling supports topological exciton bands. Lateral electron-hole separation embeds the localized exciton on the bond connecting its constituent sites rather than on either site. We demonstrate this mechanism in a honeycomb lattice, where three bond-centered charge-transfer exciton orbitals form a Kagome lattice. By solving the Bethe-Salpeter equation, we show that this emergent multi-orbital manifold supports a topological exciton flat band upon time-reversal symmetry breaking, even when the electron and hole bands are topologically trivial. The resulting band exhibits nearly uniformly distributed quantum geometry, favorable for interaction-driven bosonic states. Our results establish a general route toward topological bands of localized composite bound states and unconventional strongly correlated bosonic phases.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that charge-transfer excitons, whose spatial structure embeds them on bonds rather than sites, can form an emergent Kagome lattice manifold capable of hosting topological exciton flat bands. Even when the underlying electron and hole bands are topologically trivial, breaking time-reversal symmetry yields a topological flat band with nearly uniform quantum geometry, suitable for interaction-driven bosonic phases.
AI.motivation: Excitons have internal structure that single-particle Bloch particles lack, opening the possibility that their band topology arises from bound-state structure rather than being inherited from constituents. The key open question is how a bound state's internal structure can provide a microscopic origin of exciton topology.
AI.method: The authors demonstrate that lateral electron-hole separation in charge-transfer excitons embeds the localized exciton on the bond connecting constituent sites, creating an intrinsic manifold of symmetry-related off-site composite orbitals. They illustrate this in a honeycomb lattice where three bond-centered charge-transfer exciton orbitals form a Kagome lattice, and solve the Bethe-Salpeter equation to analyze the resulting topological bands.
AI.result: The emergent multi-orbital manifold on the Kagome lattice supports a topological exciton flat band upon time-reversal symmetry breaking, even when electron and hole bands are topologically trivial. The resulting band exhibits nearly uniformly distributed quantum geometry, which is favorable for interaction-driven bosonic states.
AI.conclusion: The findings establish a general route toward topological bands of localized composite bound states and unconventional strongly correlated bosonic phases, showing that exciton topology can emerge from internal bound-state structure rather than inherited from constituents.

title: Theory of Measurement-Altered Criticality
summary: Local measurements can alter long-range correlations in gapless quantum matter. We propose a theory of weakly-monitored Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids, a broad class of quantum critical states in one dimension. In order to address the intrinsic randomness of the measurement record, we develop a replica instanton calculation to study Born-averaged observables. We find that when measurements are relevant, average correlators of density and phase fluctuations decay at long distances as universal power laws with logarithmic corrections, a feature we argue is peculiar to measurement-induced randomness. We characterize the full multifractal spectrum of moments of correlations functions, revealing broad, strongly non-gaussian fluctuations across the ensemble of post-measurement states. We support these analytic results with matrix-product-state calculations, and provide a general picture of measurement-altered criticality for ground states described by 1+1d conformal field theories. Our results establish that physical measurements alter critical quantum states in a manner that lies beyond both forced measurements and conventional critical scaling.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a theory of weakly-monitored Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids, showing that measurement-induced randomness alters critical scaling in 1D quantum matter, producing universal power-law decay with logarithmic corrections, a full multifractal spectrum of correlation moments, and behavior beyond both forced measurements and conventional critical scaling.
AI.motivation: Local measurements can fundamentally alter long-range correlations in gapless quantum matter, but the effect of intrinsic measurement-record randomness on critical states has remained unexplored. The authors aim to provide a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding how weak monitoring modifies criticality in one-dimensional quantum systems.
AI.method: The authors develop a replica instanton calculation to study Born-averaged observables in weakly-monitored Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids, addressing the intrinsic randomness of the measurement record. They characterize the multifractal spectrum of correlation-function moments and support analytic results with matrix-product-state calculations.
AI.result: When measurements are relevant, average correlators of density and phase fluctuations decay as universal power laws with logarithmic corrections—a feature peculiar to measurement-induced randomness. The full multifractal spectrum reveals broad, strongly non-Gaussian fluctuations across the ensemble of post-measurement states, confirmed by matrix-product-state computations.
AI.conclusion: Physical measurements alter critical quantum states in a manner lying beyond both forced measurements and conventional critical scaling, providing a general picture of measurement-altered criticality applicable to ground states described by 1+1d conformal field theories.

title: Data-driven reconstruction of dynamical systems using Takens' Theorem, manifold learning, and universal function approximators
summary: Embedding theorems can be used to provide theoretical guarantees about the relation between low-dimensional observations of a system and its full-dimensional state and dynamics. Such theorems do not, however, provide guidance on observable choice, embedding construction, or methodologies to learn the mapping between the embedding and full-dimensional state. In this work, we develop an algorithmic framework, TAkens Reconstruction (TAR), to analyze and reconstruct arbitrary dynamical systems from low-dimensional time series using an integration of Takens' Delay Embedding Theorem, manifold learning techniques, and universal function approximators. We validate TAR in applications to a variety of simulated and observed dynamical systems and use it to investigate how delay vector structure impacts reconstruction accuracy. In an ecological system, we show that simple predator-prey dynamics can be reconstructed with observations taken over a wide variety of embedding time scales. In molecular dynamics simulations of the protein Villin, we demonstrate how including multiple time delays of the same observable series can be used to improve reconstruction of systems with multiple characteristic time scales. In the trade record of Vanguard S&P 500, we show how the approach exposes underlying dynamical phenomenologies in the data and accurate return predictions over short time horizons without access to full-dimensional market observations. We develop and release an open-source software package to enable the application of TAR to arbitrary dynamical systems.

AI.tldr: TAR integrates Takens' Delay Embedding Theorem, manifold learning, and universal function approximators into an algorithmic framework to reconstruct arbitrary dynamical systems from low-dimensional time series, validated on ecological, molecular dynamics, and financial datasets.
AI.motivation: Embedding theorems provide theoretical guarantees about the relation between low-dimensional observations and full-dimensional system state, but they offer no guidance on observable choice, embedding construction, or learning the mapping between the embedding and the full-dimensional state.
AI.method: The framework integrates Takens' Delay Embedding Theorem with manifold learning techniques and universal function approximators to learn the mapping between time-delay embeddings and the full-dimensional state of dynamical systems.
AI.result: Validated on simulated and observed systems: predator-prey dynamics reconstructed across varied embedding time scales; molecular dynamics of Villin protein improved by including multiple time delays to capture multiple characteristic time scales; Vanguard S&P 500 trade records reconstructed to expose underlying dynamics and produce accurate short-horizon return predictions.
AI.conclusion: The TAR framework enables reconstruction of arbitrary dynamical systems from low-dimensional time series, and an open-source software package is released for broad application.

title: Neural Flux Attachment: From Bose Condensates to Chiral Topological Matter
summary: Can one neural wave function describe both a Bose condensate and a chiral topological liquid? We introduce ChernFormer, which combines a fermionic transformer with a fixed Chern-Simons phase that attaches one statistical vortex to every particle pair. Each factor changes sign under exchange, so their product is exactly bosonic. The fixed phase changes statistics but not probability, making every bosonic learning problem equivalent to a fermionic one with the same approximation error and overlap. With enough capacity, ChernFormer can approximate any normalizable bosonic wave function on the plane at fixed particle number. A finite, smooth network still vanishes when particles meet, yet this contact hole can shrink while the wave function and condensate fraction approach those of a nodeless condensate. Following the needle-in-a-haystack target-reconstruction benchmark introduced in \cite{NazaryanGaggioliTengFu2025}, we test ChernFormer on the Kalmeyer--Laughlin ground state and its first two chiral edge states. The overlap curves stay close to unity through their largest sampled sizes, while independent amplitude and phase maps at $N=20$ for all three states recover both local Laughlin vortices and the collective edge vortex. By contrast, a continuous, nonzero product of identical particle-wise factors misses these elementary edge sectors. ChernFormer therefore provides one variational language for conventional bosonic order and chiral topological matter.

AI.tldr: ChernFormer is a neural network architecture combining a fermionic transformer with a fixed Chern-Simons phase to represent bosonic wave functions, enabling a single variational framework that handles both conventional Bose condensates and chiral topological liquids like the Kalmeyer-Laughlin state.
AI.motivation: The goal is to find a single neural wave function ansatz capable of describing both conventional bosonic order (Bose condensates) and chiral topological liquid states, which typically require very different variational representations.
AI.method: ChernFormer pairs a fermionic transformer with a fixed Chern-Simons phase that attaches one statistical vortex to every particle pair. Since each factor changes sign under exchange, their product is exactly bosonic. The fixed phase preserves probability while altering statistics, mapping every bosonic learning problem to an equivalent fermionic one. A finite smooth network creates a contact hole where particles meet, which can shrink while approaching a nodeless condensate.
AI.result: On the Kalmeyer-Laughlin ground state and its first two chiral edge states, the overlap curves stay close to unity at the largest sampled sizes. Independent amplitude and phase maps at N=20 recover both local Laughlin vortices and the collective edge vortex, whereas a continuous product of identical particle-wise factors fails to capture these edge sectors.
AI.conclusion: ChernFormer provides a single variational language capable of representing both conventional bosonic order and chiral topological matter, demonstrating universality for normalizable bosonic wave functions while recovering chiral edge physics.

title: Nitrogen Vacancy Centers in Hexagonal Diamond Exhibit Long Coherence Times
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, data and codes uploaded on QRESP after final peer review complete
summary: We show that negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in the hexagonal diamond polymorph lonsdaleite offer a route to spin qubits with enhanced coherence relative to their cubic-diamond counterparts. Using first-principles calculations, we examine two distinct defect configurations, AA, with the same symmetry as in cubic diamond and AB, with reduced symmetry. We find that the AB configuration of the NV center exhibits a finite transverse zero-field splitting, giving rise to an approximate fourfold enhancement of the Hahn-echo coherence time $T_2$ at zero magnetic field. The AA configuration, by contrast, closely reproduces the electronic structure and coherence properties of the cubic NV center. We further characterize the many-body electronic structure, vertical excitation energies, and photoluminescence spectra of both configurations, providing spectral fingerprints for their experimental identification. Our results establish symmetry-broken NV centers in lonsdaleite as promising candidates for quantum sensing and information science applications.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates via first-principles calculations that negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in lonsdaleite (hexagonal diamond) offer spin qubits with enhanced coherence. The AB configuration, with reduced symmetry, exhibits a finite transverse zero-field splitting yielding ~4x enhancement of Hahn-echo coherence time T2 at zero field, while the AA configuration mimics the cubic-diamond NV center. The authors characterize electronic structure, excitation energies, and photoluminescence spectra for both configurations.
AI.motivation: To identify new host materials for NV centers that offer improved spin coherence properties compared to cubic diamond, which could advance quantum sensing and information processing.
AI.method: First-principles calculations investigating two NV defect configurations (AA and AB) in lonsdaleite, including analysis of electronic structure, transverse zero-field splitting, coherence times, vertical excitation energies, and photoluminescence spectra.
AI.result: The AB configuration has a finite transverse zero-field splitting that produces an approximate fourfold enhancement of the Hahn-echo coherence time T2 at zero magnetic field. The AA configuration closely reproduces the electronic structure and coherence properties of the cubic NV center.
AI.conclusion: Symmetry-broken NV centers in lonsdaleite are promising candidates for quantum sensing and quantum information science applications, with the AB configuration offering enhanced coherence at zero field.

title: Next Generation of Ultra-Coarse-Graining: Self-Consistent Inference of Critical Internal States
summary: Bottom-up coarse-graining expands the length and time scales accessible to molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, but information loss can hinder accurate representation of multistate phenomena in complex biomolecular dynamics. Ultra-Coarse-Graining (UCG) projects discrete "quantum-like" extended degrees of freedom, or "internal states," onto coarse-grained (CG) molecules, extending CG model expressiveness. The rapid-local-equilibrium (RLE) approximation in UCG depends on user-defined collective variables (CVs, e.g., local density) and neglects correlations between internal states within and between CG molecules. We present Self-Consistent UCG (SC-UCG), which uses the underlying UCG interactions directly to assign internal states without designing CVs in the CG ensemble. During simulation, internal state probabilities are determined self-consistently through graph message passing. We enhance the RLE Hamiltonian with the Bethe approximation and AI-based inference to represent explicit correlations between UCG beads. For force-field training, we develop Multilayer Internal State Consistency (MISC), a machine-learning method derived from relative entropy minimization that avoids iterative sampling of intermediate force fields. We apply SC-UCG to a tetramer exhibiting a second-order symmetry-breaking phase transition from a supercritical racemic fluid to subcritical D-rich and L-rich fluids. SC-UCG captures collective switching of internal states in the subcritical region and recapitulates the phase transition across temperatures, despite being trained on a single-temperature dataset.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Self-Consistent Ultra-Coarse-Graining (SC-UCG), an enhanced UCG method that assigns internal states via graph message passing without user-defined collective variables, incorporates Bethe approximation and AI-based inference to capture inter-bead correlations, and trains force fields using Multilayer Internal State Consistency (MISC). SC-UCG successfully captures a symmetry-breaking phase transition in a tetramer system despite single-temperature training.
AI.motivation: Bottom-up coarse-graining faces information loss that hinders accurate representation of multistate phenomena in complex biomolecular dynamics. The existing rapid-local-equilibrium (RLE) approximation in UCG relies on user-defined collective variables (e.g., local density) and neglects correlations between internal states within and between CG molecules, limiting its expressiveness.
AI.method: SC-UCG assigns internal states directly from underlying UCG interactions through self-consistent graph message passing during simulation, removing the need for user-designed CVs. The RLE Hamiltonian is enhanced with the Bethe approximation and AI-based inference to represent explicit correlations between UCG beads. For force-field training, Multilayer Internal State Consistency (MISC) is developed — a machine-learning approach derived from relative entropy minimization that avoids iterative sampling of intermediate force fields.
AI.result: Applied to a tetramer exhibiting a second-order symmetry-breaking phase transition from a supercritical racemic fluid to subcritical D-rich and L-rich fluids, SC-UCG captures collective switching of internal states in the subcritical region and recapitulates the phase transition across temperatures, despite being trained on a single-temperature dataset.
AI.conclusion: SC-UCG improves the expressiveness of coarse-grained models by self-consistently determining internal states without user-defined collective variables, capturing correlated multistate behavior and reproducing phase transitions even from limited single-temperature training data.

title: Correlated topological-polarization surface states in the narrow-gap insulator FeSb2
summary: Strong electron correlations and band topology each generate rich quantum phases, but conflicting elemental requirements have largely kept them apart. Topological polarization offers a route to unite them, producing polar surface states from bonding charge without spin-orbit coupling and thereby extending band topology to correlated 3d transition-metal compounds. Here we demonstrate that epitaxial thin films of the narrow-gap insulator FeSb2 host metallic polar surface states of topological-polarization origin, governed by the strong correlations of the bulk. Nonreciprocal surface transport emerges only below the onset temperature of a correlation-driven reconstruction of the bulk Fe 3d orbital occupation, providing direct evidence of bulk-edge correspondence in a correlated topological system. Moreover, electrostatic gating drives this correlated surface across a quantum phase transition into a ferromagnetic or possibly altermagnetic state. Our results establish topological polarization as a design principle for correlated topological phases in a broad range of materials.

AI.tldr: Epitaxial FeSb2 thin films host metallic polar surface states of topological-polarization origin, governed by bulk strong correlations. Nonreciprocal surface transport appears only below a correlation-driven bulk orbital reconstruction, evidencing bulk-edge correspondence in a correlated topological system. Electrostatic gating drives the surface through a quantum phase transition into a ferromagnetic or possibly altermagnetic state.
AI.motivation: Strong electron correlations and band topology have largely been kept apart due to conflicting elemental requirements. The authors aim to unite them via topological polarization, extending band topology to correlated 3d transition-metal compounds and establishing a design principle for correlated topological phases.
AI.method: Epitaxial thin-film growth of the narrow-gap insulator FeSb2, combined with surface transport measurements and electrostatic gating to probe the correlated polar surface states of topological-polarization origin.
AI.result: Metallic polar surface states of topological-polarization origin are demonstrated in FeSb2 films. Nonreciprocal surface transport emerges only below the onset temperature of a correlation-driven bulk Fe 3d orbital occupation reconstruction, providing direct evidence of bulk-edge correspondence. Electrostatic gating drives the correlated surface across a quantum phase transition into a ferromagnetic or possibly altermagnetic state.
AI.conclusion: Topological polarization is established as a viable design principle for correlated topological phases, bridging strong correlations and band topology in a broad range of materials.

title: Simulation of positronium laser cooling using the Lindblad master equation
summary: We present a formulation and numerical results for positronium (Ps) laser cooling. The formulation is based on the Lindblad master equation and follows the time evolution of the density matrix of Ps atoms. It therefore accounts for atomic coherence, which is necessary to describe the interaction of Ps with the train of short laser pulses generated by the system developed by Shu $\textit{et al.}$ [K. Shu $\textit{et al.}$, Phys. Rev. A $\textbf{109}$, 043520 (2024)]. Using this formulation, we calculate the time evolution of the populations in each internal and momentum state and thereby quantitatively predict the momentum distribution after laser cooling. We present the representative time evolution of the internal-state populations and momentum distribution, together with a comprehensive scan of the laser parameters used to optimize the cooling efficiency. A prominent feature of the simulated distributions is sub-recoil cooling through velocity-selective coherent population trapping, a coherent effect captured by the quantum-mechanical treatment.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a Lindblad master equation formulation for positronium laser cooling that accounts for atomic coherence, allowing accurate description of interactions with short laser pulses. It predicts internal-state populations and momentum distributions after cooling, and reveals sub-recoil cooling via velocity-selective coherent population trapping.
AI.motivation: To quantitatively predict the momentum distribution of positronium after laser cooling using a formulation that accounts for atomic coherence, which is necessary for describing interactions with the short laser pulse trains generated by the system developed by Shu et al.
AI.method: The formulation is based on the Lindblad master equation, tracking the time evolution of the density matrix of Ps atoms. It computes time evolution of populations in each internal and momentum state, with a comprehensive scan of laser parameters for optimization.
AI.result: Representative time evolutions of internal-state populations and momentum distributions are presented. The simulations reveal sub-recoil cooling through velocity-selective coherent population trapping, a coherent effect captured by the quantum-mechanical treatment.
AI.conclusion: The quantum-mechanical Lindblad-based approach successfully captures coherent effects in positronium laser cooling, including sub-recoil cooling via velocity-selective coherent population trapping, enabling quantitative prediction and optimization of the cooling process.

title: Impact of spin-orbit coupling on electron correlation corrections to the density of states in anisotropic conductors
summary: We study Altshuler-Aronov-type interaction corrections to the single-particle density of states (DOS) in a strongly anisotropic 2D conductor with an open Fermi surface (FS) and weak disorder, in the presence of coexisting Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit couplings (SOCs) constrained to the longitudinal direction. The low-energy band consists of two warped sheets weakly tunnel-coupled transversely; SOC splits the sheets into helicity branches with a fixed spin axis. Working in a Matsubara space, we compute the exchange contribution in the diffusion channel with dynamically screened Coulomb interaction and an impurity ladder. The resulting DOS anomaly exhibits a dimensional crossover governed by the transverse coupling scale $\varepsilon_c$. Close to the Fermi level ($|\varepsilon-\varepsilon_F|<\varepsilon_c$), the system behaves two-dimensionally, featuring a logarithmic DOS dip whose magnitude is enhanced by intrinsic SOCs. Further from the Fermi level ($|\varepsilon-\varepsilon_F|\!>\!\varepsilon_c$), the system behaves quasi-one-dimensionally, featuring a sharper square-root singularity whose amplitude is remarkably enhanced by the SOCs. Notably, we identify a critical SOC strength at which these spin-orbit effects exactly cancel the electron-correlation correction, perfectly restoring the unperturbed density of states. Furthermore, increasing the SOC beyond this critical point inverts the sign of the anomaly entirely, yielding a positive DOS correction. This sign reversal fundamentally alters the energy dependence, such that at energies beyond $\varepsilon_F + \varepsilon_c$, the positive correction decays to smaller values as energy increases, opposite to the standard negative correction. This contrasting trend provides a distinct spectroscopic signature of SOC-modulated correlation effects.

AI.tldr: This paper theoretically studies Altshuler-Aronov-type interaction corrections to the density of states (DOS) in a strongly anisotropic 2D conductor with an open Fermi surface and weak disorder, in the presence of coexisting Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit couplings (SOCs) along the longitudinal direction. The DOS anomaly exhibits a dimensional crossover governed by a transverse coupling scale: a logarithmic dip near the Fermi level (2D-like) and a square-root singularity further away (quasi-1D-like), both enhanced by SOCs. A critical SOC strength exists where spin-orbit effects exactly cancel the electron-correlation correction, restoring the unperturbed DOS; beyond this point the anomaly's sign inverts, producing a positive DOS correction with a distinct, opposite energy dependence.
AI.motivation: To understand how intrinsic spin-orbit couplings modify Altshuler-Aronov interaction corrections to the density of states in strongly anisotropic 2D conductors with open Fermi surfaces, and to identify the resulting spectroscopic signatures of SOC-modulated correlation effects.
AI.method: The authors work in Matsubara space, computing the exchange contribution in the diffusion channel using a dynamically screened Coulomb interaction and an impurity ladder. The low-energy band is modeled as two warped sheets weakly tunnel-coupled transversely, with SOC splitting the sheets into helicity branches with a fixed spin axis.
AI.result: The DOS anomaly shows a dimensional crossover at a transverse coupling scale εc: a logarithmic dip (2D behavior) for |ε−εF|<εc and a square-root singularity (quasi-1D behavior) for |ε−εF|>εc, both enhanced by SOCs. A critical SOC strength exactly cancels the correlation correction restoring the unperturbed DOS, and beyond this strength the anomaly sign inverts, producing a positive DOS correction with opposite energy dependence.
AI.conclusion: SOC introduces a tunable mechanism that can suppress, cancel, or invert the standard Altshuler-Aronov DOS correction in strongly anisotropic conductors, providing a distinct spectroscopic signature for detecting SOC-modulated electron-correlation effects.

title: Superfluid helium
summary: We are interested in modelling superfluid helium-4, the common isotope of helium, of atomic number 4. We present a mathematically solvable toy model of the phase transition between the normal liquid and superfluid phases and use it to show how an order parameter might be obtained for the superfluid.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a mathematically solvable toy model for the phase transition between normal liquid and superfluid phases of helium-4, demonstrating how an order parameter for the superfluid phase can be derived.
AI.motivation: To understand the superfluid phase transition in helium-4 and establish a framework for obtaining a proper order parameter that characterizes the superfluid state.
AI.method: A mathematically solvable toy model is constructed to capture the essential physics of the normal-to-superfluid phase transition in helium-4, which is then used to derive an order parameter for the superfluid phase.
AI.result: The toy model successfully demonstrates how an order parameter can be obtained for the superfluid phase of helium-4, providing insight into the phase transition.
AI.conclusion: A solvable toy model offers a tractable route to defining an order parameter for the superfluid phase of helium-4, contributing to a deeper theoretical understanding of this quantum phase transition.

title: Beyond Electrons: Radiative Thermal Computing and Neural Networks at the Near-Field Limit
summary: We propose and analyze a programmable near-field radiative thermal network that emulates convolutional and recurrent operations through heat exchange. By integrating radiative thermal diodes and transistors composed of phase-change materials such as VO2 and GST, we construct two fundamental architectures: the Thermal Convolutional Neural Network (T-CNN) and the Thermal Recurrent Neural Network (T-RNN). The T-CNN executes spatial pattern recognition via temperature-dependent emissivity modulation, where each gate acts as a tunable radiative filter that amplifies or suppresses localized heat flux. The system is externally programmable via gate temperature distributions in VO2/GST, enabling weighted summation and nonlinear activation; hysteretic transitions provide state dependent responses that can be harnessed for memory. The T-RNN extends this functionality temporally, embedding radiative feedback and hysteretic phase transitions to realize memory and sequential inference. Together, these systems exhibit tri-state logic behavior, radiative gain, and non-volatile thermal storage, key attributes of physical learning. Each logical node operates without charge carriers or electrical circuits, relying solely on near-field photon tunneling between nanoscale surfaces. The resulting framework enables direct implementation of convolution, memory retention, and feedback learning within a contactless, energy-conserving platform. This study establishes the first radiative realization of thermal deep learning, revealing a new computing paradigm where temperature fields function as carriers of intelligence, uniting heat transfer, memory, and adaptive inference in a single non-electronic system.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes and analyzes a programmable near-field radiative thermal network that emulates convolutional and recurrent neural network operations purely through heat exchange, using phase-change materials (VO2 and GST) to construct Thermal Convolutional Neural Networks (T-CNN) and Thermal Recurrent Neural Networks (T-RNN), establishing the first radiative realization of thermal deep learning without charge carriers or electrical circuits.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that deep learning operations such as convolution, memory, and feedback learning can be physically realized using only thermal radiation and heat exchange, creating a new computing paradigm where temperature fields serve as information carriers in a non-electronic, contactless, energy-conserving platform.
AI.method: Integrating radiative thermal diodes and transistors made from phase-change materials (VO2 and GST) to build two architectures: (1) T-CNN, which performs spatial pattern recognition via temperature-dependent emissivity modulation where each gate acts as a tunable radiative filter; and (2) T-RNN, which extends functionality temporally through radiative feedback and hysteretic phase transitions for memory and sequential inference. The systems rely on near-field photon tunneling between nanoscale surfaces and are externally programmable via gate temperature distributions.
AI.result: The proposed systems exhibit tri-state logic behavior, radiative gain, non-volatile thermal storage, weighted summation, nonlinear activation, and state-dependent memory responses via hysteretic transitions—all achieved without charge carriers or electrical circuits.
AI.conclusion: This work provides the first radiative realization of thermal deep learning, introducing a novel computing paradigm that unifies heat transfer, memory, and adaptive inference within a single non-electronic system, where temperature fields function as carriers of intelligence.

title: Fine-Tuning Small Language Models for Reliable VASP INCAR Generation
summary: Language models can prepare VASP INCAR files from natural-language requests, but so far only large proprietary cloud models come close to handling the tightly coupled, physics-sensitive settings reliably, a dependence that fits poorly with local, high-throughput materials workflows where privacy, cost, and offline deployment matter. We show that a small language model (SLM) can close this gap. The SLM is fine-tuned on reference VASP calculations and paired with VASPGuard, a deterministic post-processor that checks syntax, workflow, and material-dependent constraints; we call the combined model INCAR-SLM. On INCARBench, a benchmark for VASP INCAR generation, INCAR-SLM built on Qwen3-4B outperforms every general-purpose LLM evaluated, exceeding GPT-5.4 by 15.55 points on the 100-point INCAR Score. Most of this gain comes from fine-tuning, with VASPGuard correcting the errors that remain. We further find that model size matters less than expected: once fine-tuning and post-processing are applied, performance saturates at a few billion parameters, and Qwen3-4B outperforms larger models in the same family.

AI.tldr: A small language model (Qwen3-4B) fine-tuned on reference VASP calculations and paired with VASPGuard, a deterministic post-processor, forms INCAR-SLM which outperforms all general-purpose LLMs including GPT-5.4 on VASP INCAR generation, exceeding it by 15.55 points on the 100-point INCAR Score.
AI.motivation: Current VASP INCAR file generation from natural language relies on large proprietary cloud models, which is incompatible with local, high-throughput materials workflows that require privacy, cost-effectiveness, and offline deployment. The authors aim to bridge this gap using small language models.
AI.method: The authors fine-tune a small language model (Qwen3-4B) on reference VASP calculations and pair it with VASPGuard, a deterministic post-processor that validates syntax, workflow, and material-dependent constraints. The combined system is called INCAR-SLM and is evaluated on INCARBench, a benchmark for VASP INCAR generation.
AI.result: INCAR-SLM outperforms every general-purpose LLM evaluated, including GPT-5.4, by 15.55 points on the 100-point INCAR Score. The majority of the gain comes from fine-tuning, while VASPGuard corrects residual errors. Performance saturates at a few billion parameters, with Qwen3-4B outperforming larger models in the same family.
AI.conclusion: Small language models combined with fine-tuning and deterministic post-processing can close the performance gap with large proprietary models for specialized scientific tasks like VASP INCAR generation, and model size matters less than expected once these techniques are applied.

title: X-ray Driven Trihydrogen Formation on Silica Nanosurfaces
summary: The trihydrogen cation ($\mathrm{H_3^+}$) initiates the ion-molecule reactions that build molecular complexity in interstellar space. Whether its canonical formation reaction, $\mathrm{H_2^+ + H_2 \rightarrow H_3^+ + H}$, proceeds on inorganic surfaces under radiation-driven ionization has remained untested. Here we drive $\mathrm{H_3^+}$ formation on hydrated silica nanoparticles using intense 1.88 keV X-ray pulses, combining ion velocity map imaging, electron time-of-flight spectroscopy, and single-particle coherent diffractive imaging to resolve this chemistry on individual particles. The self-induced surface electric field on the V/nm scale drives interfacial charge transfer and water fragmentation. This field is the dominant parameter governing the relative yields of $\mathrm{H^+}$, $\mathrm{H_2^+}$, and $\mathrm{H_3^+}$ across particle size, composition, and aggregation. Density functional theory and nonadiabatic quantum molecular dynamics simulations trace this field-driven charge transfer, directly analogous to band bending at semiconductor photoelectrodes. These results establish surface-field-driven charge transfer as a unifying mechanism between radiation dominated astrophysical environments and field-driven surface catalysis.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates for the first time that the canonical interstellar formation reaction of H3+ (H2+ + H2 → H3+ + H) can proceed on hydrated silica nanoparticle surfaces under intense X-ray irradiation. Using multimodal single-particle imaging and spectroscopy, the authors show that a self-induced surface electric field on the V/nm scale drives interfacial charge transfer and water fragmentation, governing the relative yields of H+, H2+, and H3+. DFT and nonadiabatic QMD simulations confirm this field-driven mechanism, unifying radiation-dominated astrochemistry with surface-field-driven catalysis.
AI.motivation: The trihydrogen cation (H3+) is central to interstellar ion-molecule chemistry, yet whether its canonical formation reaction proceeds on inorganic surfaces under radiation-driven ionization has never been tested. This work aims to close that gap by investigating H3+ formation on hydrated silica nanoparticles under intense X-ray pulses.
AI.method: The authors combine ion velocity map imaging, electron time-of-flight spectroscopy, and single-particle coherent diffractive imaging to resolve H3+ formation chemistry on individual hydrated silica nanoparticles driven by intense 1.88 keV X-ray pulses. They additionally employ density functional theory (DFT) and nonadiabatic quantum molecular dynamics (QMD) simulations to trace the underlying charge-transfer mechanism.
AI.result: The experiments show that the self-induced surface electric field (V/nm scale) is the dominant parameter controlling the relative yields of H+, H2+, and H3+ across variations in particle size, composition, and aggregation. This field drives interfacial charge transfer and water fragmentation, and the mechanism is directly analogous to band bending at semiconductor photoelectrodes.
AI.conclusion: The results establish surface-field-driven charge transfer as a unifying mechanism connecting radiation-dominated astrophysical environments with field-driven surface catalysis, demonstrating that inorganic surfaces can host the canonical H3+ formation reaction under radiation-driven ionization.

title: Landscape of incompressible crystals of hard-core bosons on the square-kagome lattice
summary: We investigate a hard-core boson model on the square-kagome lattice using hierarchical mean-field theory beyond the conventional unit-cell description. We show that the conventional description of the square-kagome lattice based on its smallest unit cell does not fully capture the hierarchy of incompressible states supported by the lattice, but only captures the two compact-localized-state-based phases at densities $5/6$ and $2/3$. Within our approach, we reproduce these previously established phases and uncover additional incompressible states enabled by enlarging the variational cluster. Among these, the $ρ=3/4$ phase is found to be particularly robust, which, through the Matsubara-Matsuda mapping, corresponds to a half-magnetization plateau in the spin-$1/2$ XXZ model. We further apply our approach to two experimentally relevant square-kagome compounds using exchange parameters obtained from first-principles calculations. The calculated magnetization processes are in good agreement with available experimental results and predict additional plateau structures in these materials.

AI.tldr: A hierarchical mean-field theory beyond the conventional unit-cell description is applied to a hard-core boson model on the square-kagome lattice, revealing additional incompressible states (including a robust ρ=3/4 phase) beyond the two previously known compact-localized-state phases at densities 5/6 and 2/3. The ρ=3/4 phase maps to a half-magnetization plateau in the spin-1/2 XXZ model via the Matsubara-Matsuda mapping. Applied to two square-kagome compounds with first-principles exchange parameters, the approach reproduces experimental magnetization processes and predicts additional plateaus.
AI.motivation: To fully capture the hierarchy of incompressible states supported by the square-kagome lattice, since the conventional description based on the smallest unit cell only captures two phases (at densities 5/6 and 2/3) and misses additional states enabled by larger variational clusters.
AI.method: Hierarchical mean-field theory beyond the conventional unit-cell description, applied to a hard-core boson model on the square-kagome lattice by enlarging the variational cluster. The Matsubara-Matsuda mapping connects bosonic densities to magnetization plateaus in the spin-1/2 XXZ model. Exchange parameters from first-principles calculations are used for experimentally relevant materials.
AI.result: The approach reproduces the previously established 5/6 and 2/3 density phases, uncovers additional incompressible states enabled by enlarged variational clusters, and finds the ρ=3/4 phase to be particularly robust (corresponding to a half-magnetization plateau in the XXZ spin model). For two square-kagome compounds, calculated magnetization processes agree well with experiments and predict additional plateau structures.
AI.conclusion: The conventional unit-cell-based description is insufficient for the square-kagome lattice; hierarchical mean-field theory reveals a richer set of incompressible states, including a robust 3/4-density phase. The approach successfully explains available experimental magnetization data and predicts new magnetization plateaus in square-kagome compounds.

title: Dual-Faraday-laser-pumped cesium beam clock with $7.7\times 10^{-13}/\sqrtτ$ frequency stability
summary: Compact cesium beam clocks are major frequency references for deployable timing systems. However, further improvement of their short-term frequency stability is limited by the clock signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Although two-laser optical pumping can increase the effective atomic utilization, the achievable clock SNR has long been limited by laser-induced frequency-to-amplitude noise conversion. Here, we demonstrate a compact dual-Faraday-laser-pumped (DFP) Cs beam clock enabled by a low-frequency-noise atom-referenced laser architecture. The intracavity Faraday anomalous dispersion optical filter provides inherent alignment to the Cs D$_2$ resonances, while modulation transfer spectroscopy offers suppressed frequency noise and drift. The resulting laser system supports robust turnkey operation with a Lorentzian linewidth of 2.12 kHz. The DFP Cs clock achieves a clock SNR of 46,365 in a 1-Hz bandwidth and a fractional Allan deviation of $7.7\times 10^{-13}/\sqrtτ$ , with Hadamard deviation reaching $7.7\times 10^{-15}$ at 10,000 s. This work pushes the fractional frequency stability of a compact Cs beam clock into the $10^{-13}/\sqrtτ$ regime, providing a pathway toward high-performance Cs frequency references for field-deployable precision timing, navigation, and synchronization.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates a compact dual-Faraday-laser-pumped (DFP) cesium beam clock using a low-frequency-noise atom-referenced laser architecture with an intracavity Faraday anomalous dispersion optical filter and modulation transfer spectroscopy. The clock achieves a clock SNR of 46,365 in 1-Hz bandwidth, a fractional Allan deviation of 7.7×10⁻¹³/√τ, and Hadamard deviation of 7.7×10⁻¹⁵ at 10,000 s, pushing compact Cs beam clock stability into the 10⁻¹³/√τ regime.
AI.motivation: Compact cesium beam clocks serve as key frequency references for field-deployable timing systems, but their short-term frequency stability is constrained by clock signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). While two-laser optical pumping improves atomic utilization, laser-induced frequency-to-amplitude noise conversion has long limited the achievable clock SNR, motivating the need for a better laser architecture.
AI.method: The authors develop a compact dual-Faraday-laser-pumped (DFP) Cs beam clock enabled by a low-frequency-noise atom-referenced laser system. The laser employs an intracavity Faraday anomalous dispersion optical filter for inherent alignment to Cs D₂ resonances and modulation transfer spectroscopy for suppressed frequency noise and drift, yielding a Lorentzian linewidth of 2.12 kHz with robust turnkey operation.
AI.result: The DFP Cs clock achieves a clock SNR of 46,365 in a 1-Hz bandwidth and a fractional Allan deviation of 7.7×10⁻¹³/√τ, with Hadamard deviation reaching 7.7×10⁻¹⁵ at 10,000 s.
AI.conclusion: This work pushes the fractional frequency stability of a compact Cs beam clock into the 10⁻¹³/√τ regime, providing a pathway toward high-performance Cs frequency references for field-deployable precision timing, navigation, and synchronization.

title: One-dimensional Dirac modes in the core of a pentagonal topological crystalline insulator nanowire
summary: We investigate the electronic band topology of recently fabricated pentagonal IV-VI semiconductor nanowires, which contain five radial $\{111\}$ twin planes meeting at the nanowire axis. Tight-binding calculations show that, when the bulk band structure is inverted and the twin planes in the nanowire are cationic, the spectrum contains two spatially separated helical Dirac crossings near $\overlineΓ$: one localized at the core and the other at the outer surface. When the twin planes are anionic, the corresponding spectra remain gapped. The crossings originate from the hybridization of five helical channels associated with the twin-plane edges, whose odd number leaves one Kramers pair near the nanowire axis and the other at the outer boundary. Realistic multiorbital calculations for $\mathrm{Pb}_{0.4}\mathrm{Sn}_{0.6}\mathrm{Te}$ predict well-developed core and surface modes at nanowire thicknesses of approximately 50~nm and above. These results establish pentagonal SnTe-class nanowires as an experimentally accessible realization of spatially separated helical channels bound to the axial defect and the outer boundary.

AI.tldr: This paper theoretically investigates the electronic band topology of pentagonal IV-VI semiconductor nanowires containing five radial {111} twin planes meeting at the axis. Tight-binding calculations reveal that with inverted bulk band structure and cationic twin planes, the spectrum contains two spatially separated helical Dirac crossings near Γ̄—one at the core, one at the outer surface—arising from hybridization of five helical channels from twin-plane edges. Realistic multiorbital Pb0.4Sn0.6Te calculations predict well-developed modes at ~50 nm thickness or above, establishing these nanowires as experimentally accessible platforms for spatially separated helical channels.
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize an experimentally accessible nanowire system that hosts spatially separated helical edge states at both the core (axial defect) and outer boundary, which could serve as a platform for studying topological helical channels and related phenomena.
AI.method: The authors employ tight-binding calculations to analyze the electronic band topology of pentagonal IV-VI nanowires with five radial {111} twin planes. They compare cationic versus anionic twin-plane configurations and perform realistic multiorbital calculations for Pb0.4Sn0.6Te to validate predictions at experimental length scales.
AI.result: For inverted bulk band structure and cationic twin planes, two spatially separated helical Dirac crossings near Γ̄ are found: one localized at the nanowire core and the other at the outer surface, resulting from hybridization of an odd number (five) of helical twin-plane-edge channels. Anionic twin-plane configurations remain gapped. Multiorbital Pb0.4Sn0.6Te calculations show well-developed core and surface modes at nanowire thicknesses of ~50 nm and above.
AI.conclusion: Pentagonal SnTe-class nanowires provide an experimentally accessible realization of spatially separated helical channels bound to the axial defect and the outer boundary, enabled by the odd number of twin-plane edges which leaves one Kramers pair near the axis and the other at the surface.

title: Morphology of frozen labyrinths from irreversible threshold dynamics
summary: Majority threshold dynamics, in which each agent adopts the dominant state in a weighted neighborhood, relaxes a binary field toward consensus or stripes. We study what happens when this rule is made irreversible: each agent, interacting through a Gaussian kernel on a lattice, may flip out of its local weighted minority at most once. The reversible form is threshold dynamics of Merriman-Bence-Osher type, an exactly solvable calibration in which interfaces move by mean curvature with closed-form lattice pinning and mobility. Irreversibility changes the outcome. From random initial conditions, the one-flip rule freezes balanced non-consensus labyrinths that reversible relaxation drives away. The patterned regime is a window of initial spin compositions around equal balance, narrowing as the interaction range grows, controlled by a standardized bias whose onset is independent of scale over a fourfold range. The frozen morphology is arrested coarsening: bicontinuous at balance, with a feature width that grows sublinearly and falls below the interaction range at large scales. We determine the mechanism by intervention. Fixing the initial condition while varying the update order shows that the coarse domain layout is deterministic, while the update order enters only in a secondary first-passage race that fine-tunes the wall positions the deterministic dynamics has already set. Those walls are marked by frustration: agents frozen against their own local field. This signature is identically absent from any reversible relaxation, is overwhelmingly interfacial, and carries almost none of the pattern's large-scale shape.

AI.tldr: This paper studies irreversible majority threshold dynamics where agents may flip out of their local weighted minority at most once, contrasting with reversible MBO-type threshold dynamics. The one-flip rule freezes balanced non-consensus labyrinths from random initial conditions, producing arrested coarsening with bicontinuous morphology. The pattern onset is controlled by a standardized bias window around equal spin balance that narrows with increasing interaction range. Coarse domain layout is deterministic, with update order only fine-tuning wall positions via a secondary first-passage race. Frozen walls are marked by interfacial frustration absent from reversible relaxation.
AI.motivation: To understand how making majority threshold dynamics irreversible (limiting each agent to at most one flip) fundamentally changes the outcome compared to the exactly solvable reversible MBO-type threshold dynamics, and to characterize the resulting frozen patterned states and their mechanism.
AI.method: The authors study irreversible majority threshold dynamics on a lattice with Gaussian kernel interactions, where each agent may flip out of its local weighted minority at most once. They compare with the reversible form (MBO threshold dynamics) and investigate pattern formation from random initial conditions, varying initial spin composition, interaction range, and update order. They use intervention experiments (fixing initial conditions while varying update order) and analyze frustration signatures to determine the mechanism.
AI.result: The one-flip rule freezes balanced non-consensus labyrinths that reversible dynamics would drive away. The patterned regime is a window of initial spin compositions around equal balance, narrowing as interaction range grows, controlled by a standardized bias that is scale-independent over a fourfold range. Frozen morphology shows arrested coarsening with bicontinuous structure and sublinear-growing feature width. Coarse domain layout is deterministic; update order affects only a secondary first-passage race fine-tuning wall positions. Frustration (agents frozen against their local field) is overwhelmingly interfacial and carries almost no large-scale shape information.
AI.conclusion: Irreversibility fundamentally alters threshold dynamics outcomes, producing deterministically-set frozen labyrinths with arrested coarsening. The mechanism decouples the deterministic large-scale layout from stochastic micro-scale wall placement, with interfacial frustration as the unique signature distinguishing irreversible from reversible relaxation.

title: Jsymm: A Python package for symmetry analysis of exchange tensors in magnetic Hamiltonians
summary: Symmetries of a crystal often restrict its physical properties. In particular, they determine possible forms of the tensors that describe interatomic exchange interaction, which governs a wide range of magnetic phenomena. Computationally demanding first-principles calculations of the exchange tensors can be greatly simplified by taking the symmetry constraints into account. Here, we present Jsymm, a Python package that derives the most general symmetry-compatible form of the exchange tensors directly from the crystallographic data. For any bond formed by magnetic ions, Jsymm produces the tensors of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya and anisotropic Heisenberg exchange interaction in symbolic form, as well as the tensors for all other bonds related to it by symmetry. This reduces the number of independent model parameters, dramatically lowering the computational cost of the ab initio calculations and preventing unphysical results arising from symmetry violations. The package accepts standard CIF files and provides a web interface in addition to an interactive text mode and a Python library. We demonstrate its utility on La$_2$CuO$_4$ and $α$-Fe$_2$O$_3$, reproducing known symmetry constraints and revealing additional relations between components of the exchange tensors of different bonds.

AI.tldr: Jsymm is a Python package that derives the most general symmetry-compatible form of exchange interaction tensors (Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya and anisotropic Heisenberg) directly from crystallographic data, reducing computational cost of first-principles calculations for magnetic materials.
AI.motivation: First-principles calculations of exchange tensors in magnetic crystals are computationally demanding, but crystal symmetries can greatly simplify these calculations by reducing the number of independent model parameters. This motivates developing a tool that automatically derives symmetry constraints on exchange tensors.
AI.method: The package takes standard CIF files as input and derives the most general symmetry-compatible form of exchange tensors for any bond formed by magnetic ions. It produces symbolic tensors for Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya and anisotropic Heisenberg exchange interactions, including all symmetry-related bonds. It provides multiple interfaces: a web interface, interactive text mode, and a Python library.
AI.result: The package was demonstrated on La2CuO4 and alpha-Fe2O3, successfully reproducing known symmetry constraints and revealing additional relations between components of exchange tensors of different bonds. It prevents unphysical results arising from symmetry violations.
AI.conclusion: Jsymm dramatically lowers the computational cost of ab initio calculations of magnetic exchange interactions by leveraging crystal symmetry to reduce independent model parameters, while ensuring results are symmetry-consistent.

title: Low-resistivity nitrogen-doped p-type Cu2O thin films enabled by millisecond flash lamp annealing
summary: Flash lamp annealing (FLA) provides millisecond-scale thermal processing, but its effects on p-type Cu2O and nitrogen-related defects remain poorly understood. Reactively sputtered Cu2O:N films with different nitrogen content were deposited using reactive high-power impulse magnetron sputtering and exposed to a single 1.9 ms FLA pulse at 4.9 - 11.7 J cm-2. Their compositional,morphological, structural, vibrational, electrical, and optical responses were evaluated. WDS showed no statistically significant change in total elemental composition, and XRD confirmed retention of cubic Cu2O. Nitrogen-containing films exhibited surface coarsening, shifts of the Cu2O reflections, and non-monotonic changes in the Raman band assigned to molecular N2. Nitrogen incorporation substantially reduced the as-deposited resistivity. The very low value of 0.045 Ωcm was obtained after FLA at 4.9 J cm-2, whereas higher energy densities markedly increased resistivity. Hall measurements showed increasing mobility but decreasing hole concentration. At high energy densities, the optical band gap of nitrogen-rich films widened. The results define a narrow low-energy processing window with a positive effect on electrical properties, whereas high-energy FLA modifies the structure and optical absorption edge but degrades electrical conductivity.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the effects of flash lamp annealing (FLA) on reactively sputtered p-type Cu2O:N thin films, revealing a narrow low-energy processing window (4.9 J cm-2) that improves electrical properties (resistivity as low as 0.045 Ωcm), whereas high-energy FLA degrades conductivity despite widening the optical band gap and modifying structure.
AI.motivation: Flash lamp annealing provides millisecond-scale thermal processing potential for Cu2O-based devices, but its specific effects on p-type Cu2O and nitrogen-related defects are not well understood, motivating a systematic study.
AI.method: Cu2O:N films with varying nitrogen content were deposited via reactive high-power impulse magnetron sputtering, then subjected to a single 1.9 ms FLA pulse at 4.9-11.7 J cm-2. Films were characterized by WDS, XRD, surface morphology analysis, Raman spectroscopy, Hall measurements, and optical analysis.
AI.result: WDS showed unchanged total elemental composition and XRD confirmed cubic Cu2O retention. Nitrogen-containing films showed surface coarsening, Cu2O reflection shifts, and non-monotonic N2 Raman band changes. Nitrogen incorporation reduced as-deposited resistivity; the lowest value (0.045 Ωcm) was achieved after FLA at 4.9 J cm-2, while higher energies increased resistivity. Hall measurements revealed increasing mobility but decreasing hole concentration. High energy densities widened the optical band gap of nitrogen-rich films.
AI.conclusion: A narrow low-energy FLA processing window positively affects electrical properties, whereas high-energy FLA modifies the structure and optical absorption edge but degrades electrical conductivity, providing guidance for optimizing Cu2O:N processing.

title: Rotational spectra and de-perturbation analysis for ground state ytterbium oxide, YbO
summary: A combination difference analysis of Fourier transform microwave spectroscopy (FTMW) measurements of $^{174}$YbO combined with earlier near-infrared chemiluminescence data have resulted in much improved YbO rotational and centrifugal distortion constants. These have been confirmed in a multi-isotopologue analysis of further FTMW measurements of $^{172}$YbO and $^{176}$YbO and an analysis of nuclear-size-dependent Born-Oppenheimer breakdown effects in the molecule. Multiple excited electronic states overlap with low-lying excited vibrational levels of the electronic ground state leading to irregularities in its vibrational spacings and other previously observed electronic manifolds. This has been modeled with a matrix of the vibrational levels of the ground and multiple interacting states assuming Morse potentials and including electronic Hamiltonian matrix elements mixing the states. Vibrational level overlaps were calculated numerically assuming Morse vibrational wavefunctions. The resulting de-perturbed potentials for the states inform continuing experimental and theoretical work on this and other ytterbium-containing molecules.

AI.tldr: Improved rotational and centrifugal distortion constants for YbO were obtained by combining FTMW measurements with earlier near-infrared chemiluminescence data, confirmed via multi-isotopologue analysis including Born-Oppenheimer breakdown effects. Irregularities in vibrational spacings due to overlapping excited electronic states were modeled using a matrix of coupled vibrational levels with Morse potentials, yielding de-perturbed potentials for continuing studies.
AI.motivation: To obtain much improved rotational and centrifugal distortion constants for YbO and to model the irregularities in vibrational spacings and electronic manifolds caused by interactions between the ground state and multiple excited electronic states, thereby informing further experimental and theoretical work.

A model incorporating Morse potentials and electronic coupling between the ground and multiple excited states successfully reproduced the irregularities in vibrational spacings and electronic manifolds, yielding de-perturbed potentials for the states.

title: Dissipation-induced bulk and boundary criticality in the Haldane chain
summary: We study the Haldane chain coupled to a dissipative ohmic bath. Using large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we identify a second-order quantum phase transition into an antiferromagnetic state with spontaneously broken SO(3) symmetry that is governed by an interacting fixed point with dynamical exponent $z\approx 2$. We derive a generalized string order parameter which indicates that the symmetry-protected topological ground state of the Haldane chain is stable for weak dissipation and develops a nontrivial scaling dimension at criticality. In particular, its topological edge modes display nontrivial boundary criticality that is distinct from an equivalent transition out of a trivial state; for the latter, we perform an accurate $ε$ expansion of a dissipative $φ^4$ theory with ordinary boundary conditions. Our setup realizes a spin impurity in a critical yet nonconformal antiferromagnet and paves the way for continuously tunable boundary criticality controlled by dissipation.

They derive a generalized string order parameter showing the topological ground state remains stable under weak dissipation and develops nontrivial scaling at criticality. The topological edge modes exhibit distinct boundary criticality compared to a trivial-state transition, which they analyze via an ε-expansion of a dissipative φ⁴ theory. The setup realizes a spin impurity in a critical nonconformal antiferromagnet, enabling tunable boundary criticality controlled by dissipation.
AI.motivation: To understand how symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases, specifically the Haldane chain, respond to dissipative environments, and to explore whether dissipation can drive novel quantum phase transitions and boundary critical phenomena distinct from those out of trivial states.
AI.method: The authors employ large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations to study the Haldane chain coupled to an ohmic dissipative bath. They derive a generalized string order parameter to characterize the SPT ground state, and complement numerical results with an analytical ε-expansion of a dissipative φ⁴ theory with ordinary boundary conditions for the trivial-state transition.

The SPT ground state remains stable under weak dissipation, its string order parameter acquires a nontrivial scaling dimension at criticality, and the topological edge modes show boundary criticality distinct from the trivial-state transition.
